name: Laravel notification shell
description: Receives whatever a Laravel MailMessage carries -- greeting, lines, an action, a salutation -- so every notification in an application is designed without touching a single notification class.

origin.note: The content model is Laravel's MailMessage, so this is a like-for-like replacement for the framework's notifications::email view.

subject: A message from {{ product.name }}
preheader: There is something waiting for you in your account.

greeting.description: Opening line, from MailMessage::greeting(). Laravel defaults it to "Hello!", or "Whoops!" on an error-level message.

lines.description: The paragraphs before the action button, from MailMessage::line(). One string per paragraph.

action_label.description: Button text, from the first argument to MailMessage::action(). Omit it and the button is left out entirely.

action_url.description: Where the button goes, from the second argument to MailMessage::action().

outro_lines.description: Paragraphs after the action button, which is where Laravel puts any line() added after action().

salutation.description: Sign-off, from MailMessage::salutation(). Laravel defaults to "Regards, {app name}".

subcopy.description: The fallback Laravel prints under the button so a recipient whose client eats the link can still copy the URL.

level.description: MailMessage level: info, success or error. Decides the button's colour and whether the message is banded as a problem.
